proposals.observation: 9 sessions reached intro_load in 48 hours; starts = 0, completions = 0. Every visitor who landed on the quiz page left before clicking Start. This is a copy or friction problem at the very first screen — the intro is not compelling enough to earn a click.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro headline and sub-copy to speak directly to the ICP's lived tension — earning well but not building — and add a single, low-stakes CTA label that frames the quiz as a grounded moment of honest reckoning rather than a test. Replace the current generic opener with a specific, identity-resonant hook.
proposals.current_text:
Find out your money personality
Take the quiz to discover how your relationship with money is shaping your financial future.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. So why does the money never seem to stay?
This 3-minute quiz surfaces the story beneath the money — the quiet pattern that's been running things without you noticing.
Start the honest reckoning →
proposals.impact: Converts intro-load sessions into quiz starts

proposals.observation: 3 of 13 workflow runs failed in the last 24 hours: Daily Blog Post, Weekly Monday Report, and Funnel-Hack Digest. With only 1 post queued and the daily publishing pipeline broken, the content queue will run dry within 24 hours, cutting off the primary organic discovery channel for the ICP.
proposals.proposal: Add a workflow-level on-failure notification step to each of the three failing workflows so Joel receives an immediate alert with the run URL when any content pipeline fails. This is a single file edit to the shared reusable workflow or to one representative workflow file as a template fix — restoring visibility so the root cause (likely an API key expiry or rate limit) can be diagnosed and the queue refilled.
proposals.current_text:
- name: Generate post
        run: node scripts/generate-post.js
proposals.new_text:
- name: Generate post
        run: node scripts/generate-post.js

      - name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          echo "::error::Daily Blog Post workflow failed. Check API keys and queue depth. Run: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
proposals.impact: Restores pipeline visibility; prevents silent content drought

proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has the highest open rate of the three sequences at 50%, on 8 sends. Money Avoidance and Money Worship are both lower (40% and 37.5%) on roughly double the sends. Money Vigilance is hitting the ICP's self-aware, cautious earner profile most precisely — but it has the fewest sends, suggesting either fewer quiz completions routing to it or weaker entry-point copy for that result page. Improving the result page copy for the Vigilance outcome could increase the percentage of quiz-takers routed into the highest-performing sequence.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the Money Vigilance quiz result page headline and opening paragraph to more precisely name the Vigilance pattern in language the ICP will recognise in themselves — the person who checks their balance but never acts, who is careful rather than courageous with money. Make it feel like being seen, not diagnosed, so they enter the email sequence already engaged.
proposals.current_text:
Your result: Money Vigilance
You tend to be cautious and careful with money. While this keeps you safe, it can also hold you back from building the wealth you're capable of.
proposals.new_text:
Your result: Money Vigilance
You watch the numbers. You know what's in every account. And yet — somehow — the gap between where you are and where you want to be stays exactly the same.
That's not a maths problem. That's the thing you haven't looked at yet.
The emails that follow are about that: the work underneath the carefulness.
proposals.impact: Increases Vigilance sequence entry quality and primes highest open-rate automation
